description.invocation: resnet_inference.infer(model, pixels) (resnet_inference.py:14-16): one complete forward model(pixel_values=pixels).logits under torch.inference_mode() on the prebuilt GPU-resident FP32 NCHW batch=32 pixel tensor of the offline workload row, bounded by torch.cuda.synchronize() before and after (resnet_inference.py:42-47). Excludes model loading (from_pretrained(...).cuda().eval()), pixel tensor construction from pixels.npy (resnet_inference.py:23-29), reference construction, close/negative quality checks, reference torch.save, the statistical warmup/repeats loop and result.json writing.
notes: Command provenance: user command 'python resnet_inference.py --assets /root/autodl-tmp/dev/v6-work/validation-assets/resnet18 --output /tmp/original-resnet' uses common.py argument defaults: --workloads workloads.json, --warmup 2, --repeats 5, no --profile. The script iterates both resnet_inference rows (online batch=1, offline batch=32); the user goal selects the offline batch=32 row.

Objective metric key 'latency_ms' is the exact per-sample field recorded by the source (resnet_inference.py:48): wall time of one complete batch forward between CUDA syncs. At fixed batch=32, latency_ms and images_per_second (= batch * 1e9 / elapsed_ns, same line) are reciprocals; README explicitly forbids treating fixed-batch step time and tokens/s as independent objectives, so minimizing latency_ms is the user-selected view of the row's throughput goal.

Discrete exact comparison: top-1 labels must match exactly; resnet_inference.py:33 asserts torch.equal(actual.argmax(-1), reference.argmax(-1)) and workloads.json resnet_inference.correctness.require_exact_top1=true.

Tensor comparison: full 1000-class logits via torch.testing.assert_close with atol=rtol=0.0001 (resnet_inference.py:31, common.py:74-76); corrupted-output negative control must be rejected (common.py:79-84).

Batch construction is deterministic: pixels = images[torch.arange(32, device='cuda') % 3].contiguous() from pixels.npy, which holds 3 real preprocessed public images (dog1.jpg, dog2.jpg, astronaut.jpg; FP32 NCHW 224x224, ImageNet mean/std, prepare_resnet_assets.py:47-67).

Numerics policy preserved (common.py:34-42): FP32 weights (dtype=torch.float32), TF32 disabled for matmul and cudnn, cudnn.benchmark=False, float32_matmul_precision='highest', torch.manual_seed(20261020), torch.set_num_threads(4).

The row constraint images_per_second_min_baseline_ratio=0.95 in workloads.json is scoped to the memory goal (peak_allocated_bytes, minimize) of this row; the user request is latency, so no performance constraint is attached to this objective. Peak memory (peak_allocated_bytes per sample, torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated) is still recorded by the source harness.

Single-process single-GPU workload: configure(device=0)/.cuda(); no NCCL, no distributed launch. The second GPU in the deployment inventory is not required. torch_communication collector is not requested and no required_observations are declared.
The source --profile diagnostic trace (common.py:87-105 profile_once) is separate from clean timing and absent from the user command; it is measurement infrastructure, not part of adapter.run().

assumptions: The user's 'reduce latency' objective is reported as the source sample field latency_ms (minimize); at fixed batch=32 it is the reciprocal of the row's images_per_second goal, so no source semantics are changed.
warmup=2 and repeats=5 come from common.py:24-25 argument defaults because the user command does not override them.

The memory goal's images_per_second_min_baseline_ratio=0.95 constraint stays scoped to the memory objective in the copied workload row and is not converted into a constraint on this latency objective.
device_count=1: single-process, single-GPU execution; the deployment's second RTX 4090 is not used by this workload.
Assets are used as-is from the absolute path in the user command; weights load locally (local_files_only=True) from that directory.
